passage.title: Reading Part 3 - Test 10
passage.text:
Global Water Scarcity Crisis

Water scarcity affects more than 40% of the global population, a figure that is projected to rise as climate change alters precipitation patterns and population growth increases demand. Unlike many environmental challenges, water scarcity has immediate and severe consequences for human health, food security, and economic development. Addressing this crisis requires innovative approaches to water management, conservation, and equitable distribution.
